scope: Scratch data archaeology for TITLE.DLL first-party .bss and communal holes using the shared ENG1/ENG3 copies. No canonical change. Diagnostic placeholders and layout-chosen names below are invented and are not proposals.
new_measured_rules: Unreferenced statics and unreferenced C++ globals keep their .bss storage in the natural /OPT:REF link (work_bufs, g_2a098 measured in place).

Unreferenced C tentative definitions (communals) are discarded by the natural /OPT:REF link: placeholder communals were emitted by the compiler (COFF section 0, value=size) but are absent from the map and take no space (dall/out/link.map). So a communal gap can only be alignment padding or the extent of a referenced communal, never a separate unused communal.
8+ byte .bss arrays are 8-aligned (confirmed again: canonical g_2b104[2] lands at 0x2b108).

holes.engine_references: none in either engine (no reloc target and no folded displacement in the window; ENG1/ENG3 windows are 0x404). The buffer is at offset 0 of its object in both engines (ENG1: first .bss byte after .data end 0x6e65c; ENG3: after an earlier object's 0x3f218).
holes.decision_0x800_vs_separate: separate object. The decoder's bound check uses the end pointer base+0x400 and its copy-out writes at most rows(<=32) x 2w shorts (w<=8) = 1024 bytes from the buffer, so the buffer's use is exactly 0x400 (sizeof idiom); a [0x800] array with a hand-written 0x400 bound has no support, and the engines' 0x404 window would still need another 4-byte object. Both spellings produce identical bytes; no codegen discriminator exists in any module.
holes.mechanism: static storage of a function that /OPT:REF discarded keeps its .bss (measured), consistent with the window being unreferenced in all three modules
holes.proposal: u02b70.c: g_29590 becomes the unit's static decoder buffer (ownership: offset 0 of the shared unit block in ENG1/ENG3, only user the shared decoder) and a second static unsigned char [0x400] follows it in hash order (type unknown; char array is the neutral choice). Layout names needed: buffer < second buffer < g_29d90 (e.g. g_decode_buf, work_bufs).
